title: Bill Ackman Warns Fed May Have Made A ‘Mistake’, Says AI Could Break Its Inflation Model
key_facts: Pershing Square Capital Management founder Bill Ackman wrote in a post on X that the AI boom could create an economy in which higher interest rates do not reduce demand and investment as expected.
He argued the potential payoff from winning the race to 'super intelligence' is so large that companies and governments may keep spending heavily on AI infrastructure even as rates rise.
He asked whether higher rates could themselves add to inflation if interest costs are embedded in the prices of everything.
He concluded the Fed 'might have just made a mistake'.
His concerns follow the Federal Open Market Committee raising its benchmark rate target by 25 basis points to 3.75% to 4%; the article does not date the decision.

After the decision, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said AI-related equipment and software investment has surged nearly 20% over the past year, but that the timing and scale of its impact on supply remain uncertain.
quote_evidence: “What if the old models don’t apply to the current paradigm and the Fed is wrong?” Ackman asked.
He concluded that the Fed “might have just made a mistake.”
Ackman’s concerns come after the Federal Open Market Committee raised the benchmark interest rate target by 25 basis points to 3.75% to 4%.
why_it_matters_hint: A well-known investor argues that the Fed's rate rise may not cool AI-driven demand and could add to inflation; it is his opinion.
event_date: 16 Oct 2026 (Stocktwits article, published after the Friday session; the date of the X post is not stated)
notes: REPLY STORY: Ackman answers the Fed's rate decision; the article does not give that decision's date and our recent editions did not carry it. Ackman's X post is read only through Stocktwits.
